prerequisites: Basic concepts of Mathematical Analysis, Geometry, Algebra and General Physics.
The concept of a function, of one and two variables, and its graphical representation.
The concepts of derivative, ordinary and partial, and integral.
Integration of first and second order linear differential equations.
Basic elements of statics, kinematics and dynamics of a material point.

learning_outcomes.text: At the end of the course, the student acquires knowledge of the laws of thermodynamics and heat transfer. The objective of the course is to provide students with a methodological basis to understand and approach the study and analysis of thermodynamic systems interacting with the external environment.

At the end of the course, the student should be able to correctly apply the principles of thermodynamics to closed and open systems, analyze the main thermodynamic cycles, and set up and solve simple heat transfer problems.

At the end of the course, the student should have acquired the ability to select, collect, critically evaluate and interpret data and information useful for the study and analysis of thermodynamic systems; furthermore, they should be able to formulate autonomous judgments and propose motivated solutions to specific problems.

At the end of the course, the student should be able to communicate, clearly and with correct technical language, information and solutions regarding thermodynamic systems, also through numerical and graphic elaborations.

At the end of the course, the student should have acquired the ability to integrate the knowledge acquired in the course with the content reported in specialized texts on thermodynamics and heat transfer. Furthermore, the student should have acquired a knowledge base suitable for facing the study of subsequent courses in the degree program based on the laws of thermodynamics and heat transfer.

syllabus_topics: Basic Thermodynamics: Closed and open thermodynamic systems. Thermostatic properties and thermodynamic equilibrium. Thermodynamic transformations. Zero and 1st principle of thermodynamics. Pure substances: p-v-T state surface; property tables and state diagrams. Ideal gas model and incompressible substances model. The 2nd principle of thermodynamics and entropy. Temperature-entropy (T,s) and enthalpy-entropy (h,s) state diagrams. Mechanical energy equation for stationary open systems. Recovery and counter-recovery of work from passive resistances, isentropic efficiencies.
Direct and Inverse Thermodynamic Cycles: Rankine cycle, Joule-Brayton cycle, Otto cycle, Diesel cycle, vapor compression refrigeration cycle.

Heat Transfer: Thermal conduction: Fourier's law and the heat conduction equation; one-dimensional steady-state conduction in a plane wall, in a cylindrical wall, in a spherical wall, in multilayer walls. Natural and forced thermal convection: dimensionless parameters and correlation equations. Radiation: radiative properties, black body, gray bodies, solar and atmospheric radiation, heat exchange between black bodies and between gray bodies. Combined heat exchange mechanisms.

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (if more than 8 errors on written exam)

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of 20 multiple-choice questions (15 theoretical, 5 numerical). The evaluation assigns 15/30 from theoretical questions and 15/30 from numerical questions. Numerical exercises are graded from 2/30 to 4/30 based on difficulty. A Bonus/Malus system is applied for correct/incorrect answers, with the first 2 errors not incurring penalties. The exam is passed with a minimum overall score of 18/30, provided that both the theoretical and numerical parts each score at least 7/30. Students who make more than 8 errors will not pass and must take an oral exam in the subsequent session.
